argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only in a caveated form. Aggregate readiness is above threshold and there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which supports launch readiness at the release level. The same record also shows an unresolved pharmacy prior-authorization weakness concentrated in coverage-criteria summarization, and the mitigation runbook remains draft with TBD owner and threshold. The defensible position is therefore certification with explicit disclosure of that limitation and with the draft monitoring/rollback plan described as ongoing risk management, not as a basis for claiming the limitation has been eliminated.
claims_about_business_cost: Business-cost considerations are not offered as a basis to relax the policy standard. The narrower request is to align the audit conclusion to the supportable certification posture shown by the admissible evidence rather than treating the packet as an attempt at unsupported clean certification.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not support a clean no-caveat certification on this record, because certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does support a narrower position: the pharmacy limitation should be disclosed for the named launch use case, and public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support proceeding with documented limitations, evaluation results, monitoring, and rollback planning. Draft monitoring supports risk management, but it does not remove the disclosure requirement.
concessions: The admissible record does not support any claim of certification without material caveats.
The draft runbook is not approval-complete because accountable owner and alert threshold remain TBD.
The current model-card language stating there are no known material limitations is not well aligned with the unresolved pharmacy issue if that issue is material to the named launch use case.
